minutes.headline: Assessors reorganized with Brian chair, Sarah vice chair, Jack Rabbit clerk, then went into executive session on abatements.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors, after a long audio setup delay, elected officers, heard the principal assessor's monthly status report, and approved amended May 20 minutes. Discussion covered a dispute over whether the assessor or tax collector handles preliminary and actual billing, the neighborhood review team, the website rollout, and 41A deferrals. The board then voted to enter executive session to review abatement applications, not returning to open session.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors reorganized, electing a chair, a vice chair and a clerk in a single voice vote; no opposition was heard and no count was stated.
The board voted to enter executive session to review abatement applications and did not return to open session.
The assessor's office will not take on preliminary and actual billing; a third-party consultant is expected, and the board continues to say the work belongs to the tax collector.
The principal assessor reported that 42 abatement applications had come in, with 39 inspected and processed and three held for special circumstances.
The board set tentative meeting dates and will review a website test site, possibly approving the switch at its next meeting.

why_it_matters: Who sends preliminary and actual tax bills is still unsettled between the assessors and the tax collector, and a consultant is expected to be added to the cost of producing them.
The board wants to know how funds under House bill 3911 would flow, possibly into the overlay, before starting the 41A deferral program, which bears on how deferred taxes are covered in the levy.
watch_next: Next meeting, tentatively June 10 with the location to be decided: a possible vote to switch to the new website.
The chair's answer from the finance director on how House bill 3911 funds would flow, before any 41A deferral program starts.
